text:
oliver: Heads-up — seeing token shifts / wrong outputs after long-context requests when KV eviction runs. Repro on prod: sequences with ~70k tokens then follow-up requests pick up stale KV entries, resulting in token offset misalignment. Not sure if it's a read-after-free or a tag alignment bug.

anya: which model / runtime build?

oliver: gpt-redwood-13b, runtime build 2026-03-10 (sha abc1234). Spike correlates with the tombstone-evict optimization (PR #3721) landing.

perf-bot: ALERT kv_miss_rate increased 2.3x at 2026-03-11T13:04Z; p95 latency +120ms vs baseline :warning:

kevin: can you paste a short snippet of the logs around the eviction?

oliver: here's the relevant log excerpt (redacted ids):
```
E KVCache: evict_page page_id=0x7f3a3a size=65536 tombstones=4
E KVCache: write_tombstone page=0x7f3a3a offset=4096 next_offset=8192
E KVCache: read_page page_id=0x7f3a3a offset=4097 expected_offset=4096
E KVCache: found_tag=0xdeadbeef request_id=rid-42
W KVCache: read_after_evict tentative_hit -> treating as hit
```

oliver: note the `offset=4097` vs `expected_offset=4096` — looks like a one-token shift in tag parsing.

lenka: I ran the local kv_repro harness with long-context flags and reproduced a similar misalign at ~68k tokens. It only manifests when page eviction runs while a request is still finishing up writing its tail KV page.

jess: that sounds like a race between writer advancing the page cursor and the eviction/tombstone writer. Tombstones currently store a compacted tag layout; if the writer and evictor use different alignment assumptions we can get a byte-shift.

mike: quick mitigation idea: zero the tombstoned region immediately on eviction so stale bytes can't be misinterpreted as tags. Cheap and low-risk to ship as a hotfix.

kevin: patch prototype (very small):
```
// on evict
if (page->has_tombstones()) {
  // ensure stale payload can't be parsed as a tag
  memset(page->data + tombstone_start, 0, tombstone_length);
  page->tag_base = INVALID_TAG;
}
```

kevin: longer-term fix: add a per-request generation id to entries so reads validate generation. reading code becomes:
```
if (entry->generation != current_generation) {
  // treat as miss
}
```

jess: agree on two-step plan: (1) hotfix zeroing in the eviction path, (2) stronger invariant with generation id + assertions. I'll open a PR with the hotfix and a test.

oliver: can you also add an assertion in the read path that checks tag alignment / offset modulo token_tag_size? If it fails, we should crash in staging to capture core + heap forensics.

lenka: I'll add a fuzz target that races writer/evictor loops — it reliably tripped an ASSERT in my run.

kevin: i'll run the repro harness across the last 10 runtime builds to see when this regressed and attach a bisect result.

jess: action items: open PR for hotfix (+ unit tests), add generation-id followup ticket, add ASSERT in read path (staging only), add fuzz harness job to CI. tagging @eng-sre to watch production alerts.

oliver: thanks — assigning to jess for hotfix and kevin/lenka for repro/CI. If anyone sees similar symptoms (token shifts after eviction) please drop logs here. :thumbsup:
